spans.s: 1. व the 3rd semivowel (corresponding to the vowels उ and ऊ, and having the sound of the English v, except when forming the last member of a conjunct consonant, in which case it is pronounced like w; it is often confounded and interchanged with the labial consonant ब्).
the esculent root of the water-lily
a weaver (?). a sort of incantation or Mantra (of which the object is the deity Varuṇa)
3. व ind. = इव, like, as, MBh.; Kāv. &c. (in some more or less doubtful cases).
either-or not, optionally, KātyŚr.; Mn. &c. (in gram. वा is used in a rule to denote its being optional, e.g. Pāṇ. i, 2, 13; 35 &c.)
just, even, indeed, very (= एव, laying stress on the preceding word), KātyŚr.; Kāv.
but even if, even supposing (followed by a future), Pañc. v, 36/37

(after a rel. or interr.) possibly, perhaps, I dare say, MBh.; Kāv. &c. (e.g. किं वा शकुन्तलेत्य् अस्य मातुर् आख्या, ‘is his mother's name perhaps Śakuntalā?’, Śak. vii, 20/21; को वा or के वा followed by a negative may in such cases be translated by ‘every one, all’ e.g. के वा न स्युः परिभव-पदं निष्फलारम्-भ-यत्नाः, ‘everybody whose efforts are fruitless is an object of contempt’,
[cf. Gk. ἄημι for ϝαημι; Lat. ventus; Slav. vejati; Goth. waian, winds; Germ. wâjan, wæjen, wehen, Wind; Angl.Sax. wâwan; Eng. wind.]
